text:
Maria L.: Quick sync — I'm prototyping a "per-call effective cost" mini-card for the console. Idea: show the real token cost for the last N calls (includes KV cache savings & routing fallbacks) as a single number + small sparkline. Want to validate telemetry impact and UX.
Vikram S.: heads up — if we fetch per-call attribution at full cardinality we'll blow our metrics cluster. per-session + per-route explode too. :grimacing:
Sophie: Could we do sampling and an extrapolation? e.g., sample 1% of calls but tag them with route & model sku, then infer totals. Lower cardinality’d be ok.
AJ: SQL sketch for sampled extrapolation (very rough):
```
WITH sampled AS (
  SELECT route_id, model_sku, COUNT(*) as sample_count, SUM(tokens) as sample_tokens
  FROM calls
  WHERE rand() < 0.01
  GROUP BY 1,2
)
SELECT
  route_id,
  model_sku,
  sample_tokens * (total_calls(route_id, model_sku) / sample_count) AS est_tokens
FROM sampled;
```
AJ: we can run that nightly and surface the point estimates in the card.
Kevin: also remember routing biases. sticky routing -> larger customers hit dedicated pools with different unit cost. If we only show token cost without indicating route fallback history people will be confused.
Elaine: UX idea: default to a single effective number but add a small "why" tooltip that shows breakdown: model unit cost, avg cache hit %, and % of calls that fell back to cheaper/slower model.
Maria L.: +1 to tooltip. Also want smoothing — a single noisy outlier (e.g., long chain call) shouldn't blow the card. Maybe show 95th percentile and mean toggles.
Vikram S.: Implementation note: store a tiny rollup per minute with keys (route_id, model_sku, cache_bucket) where cache_bucket is coarse (0%, 1-10%, 10-50%, >50%). That keeps cardinality bounded.
Sophie: And add an opt-in full-trace mode for customers who want exact per-call billing reconciliation. Default UI uses sampled/extrapolated data.
Kevin: One subtlety: bursts where we redirect to fallback cheaper model for capacity reasons — cost goes down but quality may drop. We should flag when fallback rate > X% in the mini-card to avoid misleading "savings".
Maria L.: Agreed. Suggest: if fallback_rate > 10% show a small orange ⚠️ and allow clicking to see the rollouts tab.
deploy-bot: deploy queued for branch feature/econ-mini-card — CI 5972 passed. https://ci.internal/5972 :shipit:
ops-bot: prototype link updated: https://console.redwood.ai/proto/econ-mini-card — note: data is from the sampled pipeline, not reconciled billing. :info:
AJ: one more thought — when extrapolating token cost we should apply model-sku unit-price at the time of the call (price history). Otherwise round-trip adjustments will be wrong.
Elaine: UI microcopy: "Effective cost: an estimate based on sampled telemetry. Click to reconcile with invoice-level data." keeps expectations clear.
Vikram S.: action items: 1) implement coarse cache_bucket rollup (eng-infra), 2) add sampling/extrapolation SQL (eng-platform/AJ), 3) add fallback-rate flag (runtime/kevin), 4) UX copy + tooltip + percentile toggle (product/elaine).
Maria L.: I'll own the feature ticket and the A/B plan. Filing: https://redwood/issue/PLAT-9134 — please add owners.
Sophie: I'll add a short ops-runbook for customers who enable full-trace reconciliation.
Kevin: timeline? I can demo a backend stub next Tue.
Maria L.: perfect. thanks all. :thumbsup:
